slides.title: Segment trees and Fenwick trees
slides.main: Store not the elements, but the answers for well-chosen sub-ranges.

captions: An array of a million numbers and a million operations
Operation one: sum (min, GCD…) on a range [l, r]
Operation two: change one element, and range answers change

slides.title: Prefix sums and their weakness
slides.main: We need a middle ground: both query and update in O(log n).

captions: p[i] is the sum of the first i elements; one pass to build
Sum a[2..5] = p[5] − p[1] = 23 − 4 = 19, in constant time
a[2] changed: all prefixes to its right are stale, up to n fixes
We need a structure where both query and update cost a logarithm

frames.text: query O(log n) + update O(log n)

slides.title: Fenwick tree
slides.sub: Cell i stores a range of length i & −i
slides.main: It all rests on the lowest set bit: i & −i.

captions: Elements are numbered from one
Cell i stores the sum of a range of length i & −i ending at i
Cell 6 has lowest bit 2: it stores a[5] + a[6]
Cell 8 has lowest bit 8: it stores the sum of all eight

slides.title: Prefix query
slides.main: prefix(i): add up cells i, i − lowbit, … until zero.

captions: We want the sum of the first seven: walk the cells, clearing the lowest bit
7 = 111₂: take cell 7 (one element), clear the lowest bit → 6
6 = 110₂: cell 6 covers a[5], a[6]; clear the bit → 4
4 = 100₂: cell 4 covers a[1..4]; clear the bit → 0, stop

slides.title: Updating an element
slides.main: update(i): fix cells i, i + lowbit, … up to the size.

captions: a[3] += 5: fix every cell whose range contains element three
Cell 3: add 5, then add the lowest bit to the index → 4
Cell 4 covers a[1..4]: fix it too and move on: 4 + 4 = 8
Cell 8 is the last; 8 + 8 is out of range, stop: three cells of eight

slides.title: Fenwick generalizations
slides.main: Range add is two difference updates; a point value is a prefix sum.

captions: Store neighbor differences: d[i] = a[i] − a[i − 1]
We want to add 5 on the range [1, 3]
Only d[1] += 5 and d[4] −= 5: two point updates
a[i] is a prefix sum of differences: a point value in a logarithm

slides.title: Segment tree
slides.sub: A node stores the answer for its range
slides.main: Node = combination of two children; n leaves give about 2n nodes.

captions: Leaves are the array elements themselves
A parent stores the sum of its two children
The root covers the whole array: about 2n nodes, height a logarithm
Like a heap in an array: node v has children 2v and 2v + 1

slides.title: Range query
slides.main: The range splits into O(log n) ready-made nodes.

captions: Query on [2, 6]: leaves 7, 1, 4, 2, 6
Fully inside: take it; outside: skip; partial: descend
Three nodes suffice: 8 + 6 + 6 = 20, about log n visits

slides.title: Bottom-up update
slides.main: Recompute the parents along the path to the root: log n steps.

captions: Change a leaf: a[3] = 1 → 6
Recompute the parent: 7 + 6 = 13
Climb further: 5 + 3 + 13 = 21
Root: 21 + 20 = 41, a path of length log n

slides.title: Any associative operation
slides.main: Associativity and a neutral element are needed; commutativity is not.

captions: Associativity is needed: (a ∘ b) ∘ c = a ∘ (b ∘ c)
Min, max, greatest common divisor: all fit
Nodes combine left to right, so the operation may be non-commutative

slides.title: Lazy propagation
slides.main: Always push the tag down before descending.

captions: We want to add 2 to every element of the left half
Node 2 is fully covered: update its sum 16 → 24 and leave a +2 tag
Before descending, pass the tag to the children: each adds 2 · length
Nodes 4 and 5 became 12 and 12, node 2's tag is cleared: work done only where we went

slides.title: Sparse table
slides.sub: Static data, minimum in constant time
slides.main: Two overlapping 2ᵏ ranges give the minimum; for sums, overlap is forbidden.

captions: Row k holds minimums over ranges of length 2ᵏ; row 0 is the array
Each cell of row 1 is the minimum of two neighbor cells of row 0
Row 2 is built from row 1 the same way: n · log n cells in all
Length 5: two overlapping fours [1..4] and [2..5], minimum 1, in constant time

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: Static: sparse table; sums with updates: Fenwick; the rest: segment tree.

captions: Prefix sums for static data; Fenwick for sums with updates
The segment tree takes any associative operation
The sparse table answers in constant time if data is static
